fields.statement: Verified at fc79973e by claude-code-d0a17d19 (verifier). run-ship-merge-tree-differs.txtar is gone (renamed to run-ship-main-dispatch-fail). go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(run-ship-main-dispatch|run-ship-main-dispatch-fail|run-ship-main-dispatch-resume|ship-main-dispatch-select)$' -count=1 -v: all four PASS, plus describe-golden and every run-ship* script; go test ./internal/api/... and ./internal/workflow/... ok. (a) run-ship-main-dispatch: local bare origin and fake gh; exactly one 'workflow run ci.yml --ref main -f sha=<merge commit>' across >=3 run-list polls with the run in_progress for the first two, push.yml (push only) never dispatched, no rerun, run reaches close-out. (b) run-ship-main-dispatch-fail: one 'run rerun 42 --failed', then 'stop: merge commit <sha>: CI failed on main: CI', no close-out. (c) ship-main-dispatch-select and run-ship-main-dispatch-resume: 'no dispatchable workflow was found' stop with no workflow run call. (d) resume script: hand-written pre-#256 state file (pr,url,branch,head,checks,merge_commit), rhiza run resume --retry dispatches once and reaches close-out. (e) select script: stops naming ci.yml for a missing sha input and, separately, for a run-name without inputs.sha, no workflow run call. (f) select script covers a tip fixing the run-name; I also reproduced (f) exactly as written by hand with a scratch build and fake gh: merge commit whose ci.yml lacks the sha input stops (exit 75), then after main gains a commit adding the sha input, ship check --main --settled dispatches 'workflow run ci.yml --ref main -f sha=<merge commit>' and passes (exit 0). Read the diff: ship check --main fetches origin first, selection reads refs/remotes/origin/main, dispatch is recorded in the state file before gh runs, reruns are keyed on the merge commit.
